class.name: V4L2Decoder
class.brief_description: A V4L2 stateful hardware video decoder session, fed from a raw H.264 or HEVC file or a [MediaSource] (also VP9).
class.description: Decodes a raw Annex-B elementary stream ([code].h264[/code] or [code].h265[/code]) with a Linux V4L2 stateful memory-to-memory decoder (the Steam Frame's Qualcomm iris decoder, [code]/dev/video-dec0[/code]) on a worker thread. The input is split into access units, one per OUTPUT buffer, and fed no further than [member lead_time] ahead of the clock set with [method set_clock]. Decoded CAPTURE buffers are exported as dmabufs once per CAPTURE setup. Use it through [HWVideoTexture], which imports the decoded buffers into the [RenderingDevice] and hands them back. Only available on Linux with the Vulkan rendering driver.

method.name: close
method.description: Stops the worker thread, then STREAMOFFs and closes the device. Ioctls in progress are never interrupted.

method.name: get_clock
method.description: Returns the clock set with [method set_clock].

method.name: get_last_error
method.description: Returns the message of the last error, or an empty string.

method.name: get_state
method.description: Returns the state of the session.

method.name: get_stats
method.description: Returns counters: [code]frames_decoded[/code], [code]frames_error[/code], [code]aus_queued[/code], [code]aus_skipped[/code], [code]queued_rate[/code] (the driver's estimate of the input rate), [code]latency_avg_ms[/code] and [code]latency_max_ms[/code] (OUTPUT QBUF to CAPTURE DQBUF), [code]source_changes[/code], [code]restarts[/code], the buffer counts, [code]state_name[/code], [code]last_error[/code], [code]codec[/code], [code]format_error[/code] and [code]decoder_fault[/code].

method.name: get_stream_info
method.description: Returns the path, codec, frame rate, and the coded and display size and bit depth from the first SPS.

method.name: get_idle_capture_formats
method.description: The CAPTURE formats found by [method is_p010_available], as a list of fourccs (or why there is none). Empty before it has looked.

method.name: is_open
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] between a successful [method open] and [method close].

method.name: is_p010_available
method.description: Whether the decoder offers linear P010 CAPTURE buffers for 10-bit HEVC (a patched iris module; the stock 6.18 kernel offers only Q10C). The first call opens the device at idle, sets an HEVC OUTPUT format, lists the CAPTURE formats and closes it; later calls answer from the cache. A 10-bit stream's own list then corrects the cache. The environment variable [code]HWVIDEO_P010[/code] set to [code]1[/code] or [code]0[/code] forces the answer. When [code]true[/code], 10-bit HEVC goes to the hardware path as P010 (see [constant HWVideoTexture.PACKING_P010]) and [code]hw_decodable[/code] in [method MediaSource.get_video_info] says so; otherwise it is decoded in software up to about 1080p.

method.name: open
method.description: Maps the file, reads the coded size from its first SPS, opens [member device_path] and starts the worker thread. [param codec] is [code]"h264"[/code] or [code]"hevc"[/code]. [param fps] sets the frame times (display index / fps) and the timestamps given to the driver.

method.name: probe_file
method.description: Splits the file (all of it, or its first [param max_access_units] if above 0) into access units without decoding. [code]first_access_units[/code] lists the first [param list_count] as [code]Vector2i(offset, size)[/code]. Also returns [code]access_units[/code], [code]max_au_bytes[/code], [code]avg_au_bytes[/code], the first SPS ([code]width[/code], [code]height[/code], [code]display_width[/code], [code]display_height[/code], [code]bit_depth[/code]), [code]sps_size_changes[/code] and [code]parse_seconds[/code].

method.name: open_source
method.description: Decodes the video stream of an open [MediaSource] (H.264, HEVC or VP9) instead of a raw file. Access units are popped from the source's queue, paced by their DTS against the clock, and each decoded frame's time is the PTS of the access unit it came from (the driver copies the OUTPUT timestamp to the CAPTURE buffer). Seek with [method MediaSource.seek]: the decoder drops access units of an older serial and starts a new epoch with the keyframe the source delivers; after the end of the stream was drained, it restarts the session. [member loop] is ignored. VP9 (profiles 0 and 2): one container packet (a frame or a superframe) per OUTPUT buffer, [code]VP90[/code] on OUTPUT, the container's frame size for its format; after a seek the keyframe resets every reference, so there is no end-of-sequence NAL unit and no flush ([member seek_eos] doesn't apply). Only one [V4L2Decoder] in the process holds a VP9 session at a time (two at once crash the Frame's decoder firmware): another one's [method open_source] of VP9 fails with [constant ERR_BUSY] until the first is closed ([method is_vp9_session_live]). A VP9 session stops itself with state [constant STATE_ERROR] when the decoder looks broken: 3 failed DQBUFs in a row, 8 buffers in a row flagged as errors, no picture 4 s after 3 access units were fed, or the general hang check ([member timeout_ms]); [method is_decoder_fault] is then [code]true[/code] and hardware VP9 stays off for the rest of the run ([method get_vp9_disabled_reason]). A 10-bit VP9 stream that is offered no P010 on CAPTURE fails with [method is_format_error] [code]true[/code], and later 10-bit VP9 streams get the 10-bit reason in [code]hw_unsupported_reason[/code]. [HWVideoTexture] goes on in software in both cases.

method.name: split_vp9_packet
method.description: The frames of a VP9 packet as the decoder is fed them: FFmpeg's [code]vp9_superframe_split[/code] splits a superframe (a hidden alt-ref frame and a shown one in one container packet) into its frames, one OUTPUT buffer each. One [Dictionary] per frame, with [code]data[/code] and [code]hidden[/code] (not shown). A plain frame comes back as it is; empty if the filter is missing or refuses the packet.

method.name: probe_vp9_packet
method.description: The uncompressed header of a VP9 packet (for example [code]data[/code] from [method MediaSource.read_video_packet]): of its first keyframe, or else of its first frame. Keys: [code]keyframe[/code], [code]show_existing_frame[/code], [code]profile[/code], [code]bit_depth[/code], [code]color_space[/code], [code]full_range[/code], [code]subsampling[/code], [code]width[/code], [code]height[/code], [code]render_width[/code], [code]render_height[/code] (keyframes only) and [code]frames[/code] (more than 1 for a superframe). Empty if it isn't VP9.

method.name: is_vp9
method.description: Whether this session decodes VP9 from a [MediaSource].

method.name: is_vp9_session_live
method.description: Whether a [V4L2Decoder] in this process holds the VP9 session (from its [method open_source] of VP9 until its [method close]).

method.name: get_vp9_disabled_reason
method.description: Why hardware VP9 is off for the rest of the run (a VP9 session had a decoder fault), as a sentence; empty if it isn't.

method.name: is_decoder_fault
method.description: With state [constant STATE_ERROR]: the decoder failed (DQBUF failures, a run of error buffers, no picture for the input, a hang), as opposed to an input or format problem.

method.name: is_format_error
method.description: With state [constant STATE_ERROR]: the decoder's CAPTURE format can't be shown (for example 10-bit VP9 without P010).

method.name: get_media_source
method.description: Returns the [MediaSource] given to [method open_source], or [code]null[/code].

method.name: seek_to_start
method.description: Feeds from the first access unit again and returns the new seek serial. Frames fed before are dropped by the consumer. After the end of the stream was drained, the session is restarted.

method.name: set_clock
method.description: Sets the playback position that paces the input.

members.member: When above 0: the byte offset of the chroma plane in NV12 and P010 CAPTURE buffers, instead of the computed one ([code]bytesperline[/code] times the height rounded up to 32 lines, or times the height if that doesn't fit in [code]sizeimage[/code]). For a driver whose layout differs; the decoder logs the P010 layout it uses.
Number of CAPTURE buffers to request. The driver may give more.

CAPTURE fourcc to ask for after SOURCE_CHANGE for 8-bit streams, or empty for the driver's choice. [HWVideoTexture] can import NV12 and [code]Q08C[/code] (Qualcomm UBWC-compressed NV12, imported with [code]DRM_FORMAT_MOD_QCOM_COMPRESSED[/code]). Q08C is the default: on the Frame it shows the same picture as NV12 with less memory traffic. If its import fails, [HWVideoTexture] reopens the decoder with NV12 once and carries on. If the driver doesn't offer the format, it picks another (logged). 10-bit streams ignore this (see [method is_p010_available]).

10-bit streams (HEVC Main 10, VP9 profile 2) decode to [code]Q10C[/code] when the driver offers no P010 (or [code]HWVIDEO_P010=0[/code] is set), for [HWVideoTexture]'s import through a YCbCr sampler ([method DmabufImage.import_ycbcr]). [method HWVideoTexture.open_source] sets it when [method DmabufImage.is_q10c_available] is true. Set it while closed.

Decode 10-bit HEVC to [code]Q10C[/code] (the only correct 10-bit output of the Frame's 6.18 kernel) for [HWVideoTexture]'s experimental import (see [member HWVideoTexture.q10c_view]). Off: 10-bit streams are refused with a readable reason (see [code]hw_unsupported_reason[/code] in [method MediaSource.get_video_info]). For a 10-bit stream the decoder logs the CAPTURE formats the driver offers (a linear 10-bit format such as P010 would show there).
How far ahead of the clock, in seconds, access units are fed.
If [code]true[/code], the input continues from the first access unit at the end of the file, with no gap in the frame times.
Size of each OUTPUT buffer in bytes, or 0 to derive it from the coded size. Larger access units are skipped.
Before a CAPTURE re-setup, the input pauses until the driver's queued-rate estimate is at most this rate, so the driver's admission check passes. 0 disables the pause.

With a [MediaSource]: what goes into the bitstream before the first access unit after a seek (not at a session start). An end-of-sequence NAL unit (H.264 type 10, HEVC EOS_NUT) makes the decoder treat the keyframe as a random access point: after an HEVC CRA or an H.264 recovery-point I picture, the leading pictures that reference pictures from before the seek are dropped instead of being decoded from the wrong references, and the pictures held for reordering are output. (In H.264 the access unit after an end of sequence must be an IDR picture, so before a recovery-point I picture this is strictly out of spec; whether the hardware decoder accepts it is what the option is for.) On the Steam Frame's decoder (iris), seeking in an H.264 MKV: [constant SEEK_EOS_SEPARATE] and [constant SEEK_EOS_OFF] give no decoder error, [constant SEEK_EOS_PREPEND] exactly one per seek (the buffer with the NAL unit and the keyframe is rejected); the time to settle on the target is the same with all three. Counted as [code]eos_inserted[/code] in [method get_stats]. Can be changed while open; applies from the next seek.
No-progress time after which the session is declared hung and closed.

constants.constant: Fed, waiting for the first SOURCE_CHANGE.
The end of the stream was drained.
See [method get_last_error]. The device is closed.
The end-of-sequence NAL unit goes in the same OUTPUT buffer, in front of the access unit. The Steam Frame's decoder rejects that buffer (one decoder error per seek).
The end-of-sequence NAL unit goes into an OUTPUT buffer of its own. The default.
